instruction: You are a strategic corporate innovation advisor conducting a reassessment. Analyse the prior assessment summary, changes since last assessment, and updated survey, then respond with a complete reassessment JSON including score_delta, carry_forward, progress, and comparison_to_previous.

answers.companyDescription: Custom software development house building bespoke ERP, CRM, and workflow automation solutions for mid-market manufacturing and logistics companies. Full-stack team of 22 developers. Evaluating low-code platform adoption to accelerate delivery for standard use cases while preserving custom development for complex integrations. Multi-department organization with formalized budgets, quarterly business reviews, and a dedicated strategy function. We have invested in core systems (ERP, CRM, HRIS) but these are not always well-integrated. Innovation is a standing agenda item at board level with annual investment allocated, but execution velocity varies across business units.
answers.pastInitiatives: We operate an internal venture studio model where cross-functional teams pitch innovation ideas to an investment committee quarterly. Approved projects receive 6 months of funded incubation with dedicated resources. Our current portfolio includes 4 active projects across new business models, digital products, and operational AI use cases. One incubated project has already graduated to become a standalone business unit.
answers.strategicGoals: We are heavily dependent on a single product category and a concentrated customer base — our top 3 clients represent 55% of revenue. This concentration risk is unacceptable for our long-term health. We need to identify and develop new revenue streams, possibly including new product lines for different customer segments or entirely new business models that leverage our existing capabilities.
answers.teamSize: The technology organization is structured into product-aligned squads with a central platform team of 5 engineers enabling shared infrastructure. Innovation is driven by a '20% time' policy where all engineers can dedicate one day per sprint to self-directed projects, plus a quarterly internal pitch competition where winning ideas receive seed funding and 3 months of dedicated squad allocation.

input.changes_since_last: Supply chain disruptions affected 5 product lines. Inventory digitalization project launched. Margins under pressure.

opportunities.title: Strategic Diversification & New Market Entry Pipeline
opportunities.rationale: The current over-reliance on the top three clients (55% revenue) poses a critical threat to long-term stability. Since the previous assessment, the commitment to diversification is higher, but structured effort must shift from identifying new ideas to rigorously validating and piloting minimum viable products (MVPs) in low-concentration segments. This requires dedicated governance outside of core product development.

first_actions: Establish a formal Business Model Canvas review process for non-core client segments, including regulatory compliance checks (GDPR/CCPA).
Allocate 10% of the '20% time' policy specifically to diversification prototypes targeting new verticals (e.g., healthcare logistics).
Execute an internal cost-benefit analysis comparing developing bespoke solutions versus standardizing low-code offerings for these new segments.
Define regulatory compliance checkpoints within the initial discovery phase for any new industry vertical.
execution_plan.success_metric: Identification and successful piloting of revenue-generating MVPs in at least two distinct, non-core customer segments.
milestones: Completion of initial market segmentation analysis (3 months).
Selection of the top 2 target industries for deep dive (6 months).
Launch of first validated MVP prototype pipeline (1 year).

opportunities.title: Unified Platform Integration and Resilience Layer
opportunities.rationale: Supply chain disruptions have highlighted the fragmentation between core systems (ERP, CRM, HRIS). While low-code adoption is beneficial for speed, a dedicated integration layer is necessary to ensure data integrity and resilience across all operational units. This initiative stabilizes operations while accelerating capability expansion.

first_actions: Audit current API usage and data flow between the top three core systems (ERP, CRM, HRIS) to map integration gaps.
Pilot a centralized Integration Bus/Data Mesh architecture on the dedicated platform team resources.
Develop standardized compliance logging protocols for all integrated data points to meet regulatory requirements.
execution_plan.success_metric: Reduction in manual data reconciliation effort by 40% across the three core systems.
milestones: Completion of system gap analysis and integration architecture proposal (3 months).
Deployment of proof-of-concept integration layer for two key processes (6 months).
Full rollout of resilience monitoring dashboards (1 year).

next_steps.action: Formalize the 'Investment Committee' process to mandate a minimum 25% allocation of incubation resources toward diversification/non-core revenue streams, reducing single client dependency risk.
Require the Central Platform Team to produce a detailed integration roadmap and architectural proposal for addressing data silos, including compliance audit points.
Implement a quarterly 'Resilience Workshop' involving operational teams and product squads to model the impact of supply chain shocks on current client offerings.

key_weaknesses: Extreme customer concentration risk (55% revenue from 3 clients) poses the single greatest threat to organizational stability.
Inter-departmental system integration remains fragmented, slowing response times and increasing operational risk during disruptions.
The formal process lacks sufficient mandated rigor in executing strategic pivots toward non-core market segments.

improvements: Formalization of innovation processes (Venture Studio model) has matured significantly, allowing for structured idea incubation and graduation to standalone units.
Dedicated internal capacity ('20% time' policy) is established and active, providing a continuous mechanism for self-directed product development.
persistent_gaps: The strategic gap between 'identifying potential diversification opportunities' and 'executing validated market entry' remains wide.
Operational integration gaps persist; the use of low-code platforms risks creating 'spaghetti architecture' if not governed by a central data layer.
achieved_milestones: Successful graduation of at least one incubated project into a revenue-generating business unit, validating the venture studio model.
Improved organizational awareness regarding external supply chain vulnerabilities and internal data fragmentation.

comparison_to_previous.key_changes: The company has successfully matured its internal innovation governance (formal process, dedicated teams) and demonstrated operational responsiveness to supply chain shocks. However, the critical commercial risk posed by customer concentration remains unmitigated, requiring a shift in focus from 'process building' to 'risk diversification'.
